commit_message:
Be fully RFC 5280 pedantic about notAfter

May as well catch this case too. Any such certificate which
is valid for the notBefore at the time in quesion should be
considered valid no mater what the time is even if the system
time has been set to something beyond the range of ASN1_TIME values.

Reviewed-by: Neil Horman <nhorman@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Saša Nedvědický <sashan@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/28623)

fix_commit.message: Fix heap-buffer-overflow in CI fuzzing tests
fix_commit.author: Bernd Edlinger

findings.title: Heap-buffer-overflow via strcmp() on non-NUL-terminated ASN1_STRING data in ossl_x509_check_cert_time
findings.message: The code added to ossl_x509_check_cert_time() (and mirrored in ossl_x509_check_certificate_times) treats the raw data buffer returned by ASN1_STRING_get0_data() on the certificate's notAfter field as a NUL-terminated C string and passes it to strcmp() to compare against the literal "99991231235959Z". ASN1_STRING objects are NOT guaranteed to be NUL-terminated and their length is tracked explicitly via the ASN1_STRING.length field, not by a terminating NUL byte. An attacker-supplied (or malformed) certificate can craft a notAfter ASN1_TIME whose underlying buffer is shorter than 15 bytes and does not contain a NUL terminator within the allocated buffer, causing strcmp() to read past the end of the heap allocation while searching for a terminator that never appears within bounds. This results in a heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read), which was discovered via OSS-Fuzz/CI fuzzing of certificate parsing and verification.
findings.suggestion: Do not treat ASN1_STRING data as a NUL-terminated C string. Explicitly check the ASN1_STRING length equals the expected literal length (15 for "99991231235959Z") before comparing, and use memcmp() instead of strcmp() to compare exactly that many bytes.

ground_truth.root_cause: Assuming ASN1_STRING_get0_data() returns a NUL-terminated string and using strcmp() on it without first validating the string's explicit length field, when ASN1_STRING objects only guarantee explicit length tracking, not NUL termination.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Heap-buffer-overflow via strcmp() on non-NUL-terminated ASN1_STRING data in ossl_x509_check_cert_time
